title: Atlantis as an island empire on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge

tellings.quote: If we take Plato's account as being legitimate to some extent, he's describing an a midatlantic island-based empire with sophisticated maritime and navigational skills.
I think the Azors is interesting.
tellings.difference: Told by Michels as host, crediting Carlson, with no detail on the empire.
tellings.link_reason: Same theory that Atlantis lay in the Azores on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, credited to Randall Carlson.

related.note: Same subject (where Plato's Atlantis was) but places it in Antarctica rather than on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a competing claim.

plain: Atlantis, the lost civilisation described by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, may have been a real island empire in the middle of the Atlantic, near the undersea mountain chain called the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, with great seafaring and navigation skills. The researcher Randall Carlson argues this in his Atlantis lecture, saying that if Plato's account is "legitimate to some extent" it describes "a midatlantic island-based empire." Michels later credits Carlson and says he finds the Azores, a group of Atlantic islands, interesting as a candidate.
